findings.affected_surface: Error reporting side effects during Ruby process exit cleanup
findings.old_behavior: During Ruby process exit (rb_ec_teardown), if rb_vm_trap_exit() raises an exception (TAG != NONE), the trap error was silently discarded. ec->errinfo was not preserved. After EC_POP_TAG, rb_ec_exec_end_proc would run, potentially overwriting errinfo with END handler errors. EXIT trap exceptions could be lost entirely.
findings.new_behavior: During Ruby process exit, if rb_vm_trap_exit() raises an exception, the trap error is saved in a local trap_errinfo variable. ec->errinfo is cleared to Qnil before END procs run. After END procs complete, the trap error is reported via error_handle() and ec->errinfo is restored to trap_errinfo. This ensures EXIT handler exceptions are preserved and reported after END block handlers, without loss.
findings.compatibility_reason: The side effect of error reporting during Ruby process exit cleanup changes observably. Any Ruby program that registers both Signal.trap(:EXIT) and END/at_exit blocks which raise exceptions will produce different error output after this patch. Previously, EXIT handler exceptions could be silently lost; now they are always reported. END handler error output may also differ because shown_causes are shared via add_shown_cause() in eval_jump.c to prevent duplicate cause chains. This affects the externally visible diagnostic output during crash/exit reporting.
findings.why_not_internal_only: rb_error_write and rb_ec_exec_end_proc are non-static functions. The error output change is visible to any Ruby program, script, or test that observes error output during process exit. The change in diagnostic output affects all users of the Ruby interpreter during abnormal exit.
findings.uncertainty: The exact before/after error output difference depends on specific exception types and ordering. For programs without both EXIT traps and END blocks that raise, behavior is identical.
findings.recommended_review: Verify that error output during process exit with EXIT traps and END blocks does not break downstream tooling that parses Ruby error output.
findings.test_recommendation: Create Ruby scripts with combinations of Signal.trap(:EXIT) raising exceptions and multiple END blocks raising exceptions. Compare before/after stderr output for correctness and completeness.

findings.affected_surface: Exception reporting during END handler + EXIT trap error handling
findings.old_behavior: When multiple END/at_exit handlers raised exceptions, each handler's error was independently reported via error_handle() without tracking already-shown causes. This could cause duplicate cause chain output in error messages. EXIT handler errors were processed by rb_ec_teardown before END handlers, potentially being lost when END handlers also failed.
findings.new_behavior: END handler errors now share a common shown_causes accumulator (add_shown_cause in eval_jump.c). When an END handler raises, its errinfo is recorded as a shown cause before the next handler runs, preventing duplicate cause reporting. EXIT handler errors are now processed AFTER END handlers in rb_ec_teardown, ensuring they are visible. The error_handle_with_shown_causes function in eval_error.c accepts an external shown_causes pointer to enable this sharing.
findings.compatibility_reason: Exception reporting during Ruby process cleanup changes observably. Programs with multiple END blocks that chain exceptions AND an EXIT trap will see different error messages: duplicate causes are eliminated, and EXIT trap exceptions now appear in output. Test suites that assert on specific exception messages or counts during exit will be affected. The error_handle function is now a thin wrapper around error_handle_with_shown_causes, preserving the public API signature but changing internal error routing.
findings.why_not_internal_only: The rb_error_write function (public/non-static) and rb_ec_exec_end_proc (public) both participate in the error reporting path during Ruby process exit. The change in exception deduplication and reporting order is directly observable in process exit error output, which is the primary diagnostic mechanism for Ruby users.
findings.uncertainty: Whether a specific test suite breaks depends on exact error output assertions. Programs without both END blocks and EXIT traps are unaffected.
findings.recommended_review: Review test cases in test/ruby/test_exception.rb that assert on exception output during END/EXIT handlers. Verify the new test_multiple_error_handle and test_cause_in_exit_handler tests match expected behavior.
findings.test_recommendation: Run the existing test/ruby/test_exception.rb test suite and verify the new tests pass. Also create standalone Ruby programs with various combinations of END blocks and EXIT traps to validate error output completeness.
